author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Lindsay Clancy is scheduled to return to Plymouth Superior Court on Tuesday, her first appearance there since a jury deadlocked and Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial on Sept. 4.

The Associated Press reported that several defense motions could be addressed at the hearing. Attorney Kevin Reddington is asking the judge to dismiss the criminal case rather than allow a second trial, including through a double-jeopardy argument tied to the court’s handling of a juror who favored conviction.

The first trial ended with the jury split 11-1 in favor of acquitting Clancy of murder charges, according to AP. Her defense has argued that postpartum psychosis left her unable to understand or control her actions; prosecutors argued that she knew what she was doing when she killed her three children in 2023.

Tuesday’s hearing could also clarify whether Plymouth County prosecutors will seek another trial on first-degree murder charges, pursue lesser charges or drop the case. The prosecution has not announced a final decision, and Clancy remains charged while the judge considers the pending motions.
The defense requests are arguments, not rulings. The court has not dismissed the case, barred a retrial or made a new finding about Clancy’s criminal responsibility.
dek: A Tuesday hearing could determine whether prosecutors pursue a second trial after jurors deadlocked in the Massachusetts mother’s case.
headline: Lindsay Clancy returns to court as defense fights second trial
seoTitle: Lindsay Clancy returns to Plymouth court after mistrial
seoDescription: A Plymouth hearing could determine whether prosecutors pursue a second trial after the Lindsay Clancy jury deadlocked.
